subject: sociology
title: Many Kinds of Family
welcome_lead: Step inside Britain's living rooms and meet the many family types that have replaced the old cereal-packet nuclear family.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure on family types: nuclear, extended, reconstituted, single-parent, beanpole.
final_note: You can now name and define six family types — the spine of any diversity essay.

concepts.def: Two parents and their dependent children only.
One parent raising one or more children.
Long, thin: many generations, few children.
Couple living together without being married.

walkthroughs.body_html: Once seen as the 'norm', the nuclear family is two parents and dependent children. Parsons called it the perfect 'fit' for industrial society because it is small and mobile.
Rising divorce since 1969 led to more single-parent and reconstituted families. About 1 in 7 UK families with dependent children are lone-parent, the vast majority headed by a mother.
People live longer and have fewer children, producing a beanpole: four generations alive but only one or two children per generation. This raises questions about elderly care.

mcqs.q: A 'reconstituted family' is best described as:
options: Two parents, biological children only
A blended step-family
A single parent and one child
Three generations under one roof
Married and living together
Couple living together unmarried
Couple living apart together
Two friends sharing a flat
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
A reconstituted family is one that has been put back together after divorce.
A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
A family formed when partners with children from previous relationships come together — a 'blended' or step-family — one of several family forms recognised in family diversity literature.

options: It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.

It is a recent invention of capitalism.

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: A reconstituted family is a family living in temporary housing.
